methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $26M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
Orchard Robotics, founded by Charlie Wu, is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $25.8M to date. The valuation analysis benchmarks against a comparable universe of 9 private peers and 1 public company in the robotics and manufacturing sector, including later-stage companies such as Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B Series B), Dexterity ($1.6B Series B), and Generalist AI ($2.0B Series B), as well as earlier-stage reference points like Walden Robotics ($1.1B Seed).

Two triangulation methods were applied. The stage-progression method, using total capital raised as a valuation proxy, applies a 2.0x multiplier typical for Series A progression, yielding $52M. The peer-median method derives a $1.7B implied valuation from the median across the four sampled peers (range: $1.1B–$2.0B). The disparity reflects the heterogeneity of the peer set, which spans from Seed to Series B stages.

The triangulated valuation range is $44M (low) to $2.0B (high), with a median of $876M. The wide spread reflects material uncertainty regarding Orchard's product maturity, market traction, and how its specific stage and risk profile map onto the available comparables. The peer-median method likely overstates valuation due to later-stage bias in the sample; stage-progression likely understates it by treating capital raised as a floor. A defensible range for Series A pricing would skew toward the lower quartile of the peer distribution, approximately $100M–$400M, pending deeper diligence on unit economics and market adoption.
